children: Broadcom shares were up about 2% on early Monday, as investors responded to renewed confidence in the company's AI chip outlook.

The move follows CEO Hock Tan's recent rejection of concerns that slower AI development could weaken demand for Broadcom's custom processors and networking products. Tan has maintained that AI infrastructure spending should continue to support the business, particularly as inference workloads expand.

Broadcom's latest quarterly figures provide additional context. The company generated $29.6 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, up 86% from a year earlier, while AI semiconductor revenue climbed 221% to $16.7 billion.

The company is also looking to customer demand from Anthropic and other AI developers. Anthropic is expected to become Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027, while management projects AI semiconductor revenue of about $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028.
The latest rebound comes after Broadcom shares faced pressure alongside other AI-related stocks amid debate over the pace of future AI spending,

title: Broadcom Stock Jumps. Anthropic Could Become Its Biggest Custom Chip Customer
